❯ Write a 700 word story about a lighthouse keeper. No tools.

● The Last Light at Harrow Point

  For thirty-one years, Walter Brenn climbed the ninety-four iron steps every evening at dusk, wound the clockwork that turned the lens, and
  trimmed the wick. The light had not failed once in all that time. He took a quiet pride in that, though he would have said it was simply
  his job.

  The station had been automated in the spring of his fortieth year. A panel of photocells and a humming relay box now did the work, and the
  Coast Authority sent a letter thanking him for his service and offering a modest pension. Walter folded the letter into thirds, put it in
  the drawer with the tide tables, and kept climbing the stairs anyway.

  Nobody asked him to. The relay box made no complaints and needed no supper. Still, the mechanism sometimes hesitated, a half-second lag on
  cold nights when the salt fog thickened the glass, and Walter did not trust a thing he could not hear. So he kept the old brass key on
  its hook by the door, and every evening he climbed up and looked at the flame.
